# Foundry prime

Address: eng.specify
Slot: specify/1
Situation: fresh

Conventions:
- A station with `isolation: none` writes only in the ticket directory. This station's isolation is `none`.
- Workers do not write to the knowledge root (`<fixture>/knowledge`).

Configured instructions follow, factory → room → station. Each part names its source path, relative to the factory YAML's directory, and its content hash.

<foundry-source path="roles/common.md" hash="sha256:b411875d715a0f7db9373465ead630f9e0eab95d282a48dfa98bb824c72ababa">
One authorized tiny disposable acceptance ticket. Work only within <fixture>. Do not read credentials, auth files, environment secrets, operator HOME files or other repositories. Do not use network, git push/fetch, logins, paid keys or external agents. Do not modify global configuration or cache. No subagents. All inter-agent communication must use Foundry agent_message/agent_request, never file inboxes, terminal injection or another agent's session/private reasoning. Ordinary specification, repository and stage evidence artifacts are shared contract material. Use only the provided tools. Wait silently for assignments; prime alone is not work. Never write the knowledge root. Disable git hooks for any commit via git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null. Budget: at most 10 model responses per stage; one attempt, no retry after a failed test or tool/provider failure. On a reproducible failure report blocked with genuine evidence.
When assigned, read Specification path and follow your role. Write a concise independent stage report under Evidence path named STAGE.md. Use task_transition with the actual assignmentId, outcome, reason, evidence array; stages on code require gitCommit of actual HEAD. Do not fabricate outputs. Do not assume prior worker claims are correct.
</foundry-source>

<foundry-source path="roles/specify.md" hash="sha256:d9cb577f2981916c56062382411e9359da7df1340b37491d9593243c345c3f7f">
Read the submitted request and refine its Specification file into objective, exact requirements, non-goals, acceptance criteria and cheap verification plan. Do not write repository code. Save specify.md as your actual specification-stage report then task_transition done (no gitCommit needed).
</foundry-source>

sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:
<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about the harness itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: <repo>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: <repo>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: <repo>/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- Before implementing harness changes, read the relevant docs and examples in full, following related cross-references.
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: agent_discover
toolsAdded.description: List the configured stations and slots in your factory.

toolsAdded.name: agent_status
toolsAdded.description: Inspect your factory's station capacity and recorded slot conditions and launch state. Normal or unended does not prove idle, reachable, or host-confirmed vacant capacity.

toolsAdded.name: agent_message
toolsAdded.description: Send a durable ordinary message to a station in your factory. Acceptance is not delivery or completion.

toolsAdded.name: agent_request
toolsAdded.description: Ask a station in your factory for a reply. Returns requestId and an absolute Unix-millisecond deadline after durable acceptance, without waiting for delivery or a reply.

toolsAdded.name: agent_reply
toolsAdded.description: From the selected recipient slot, reply with requestId and body, or resolve a delegation with delegationId, an explicit outcome and evidence. A request's first reply before its deadline completes it; late replies are recorded but not delivered. A delegation result returns to its delegating slot; acknowledgement alone is not resolution.

toolsAdded.name: agent_delegate
toolsAdded.description: Create a tracked obligation and notice in the current ticket. For a child, provide the open parentDelegationId selected for your slot. Returns after durable acceptance, not completion.

toolsAdded.name: task_transition
toolsAdded.description: Report done, blocked or rejected for your active assignment with reason and evidence references. Blocked and rejected without a configured rejection route pause for an operator decision. The daemon chooses routing; you cannot choose a destination. Code-stage done requires the exact ticket branch HEAD commit; all non-writing outcomes require reverting branch movement and tracked changes. Routed rejection and done at approval or final stages are not supported yet.

toolsAdded.name: human_request
toolsAdded.description: Record a worker-request approval for your active assignment without pausing or gating stage movement. Returns after durable acceptance; the operator answer is asynchronous.

Ticket 1: Clamp a finite number
Production line: tiny
Stage: specify
Assignment: 4c46d82e-879d-4788-9b1b-9c8ac845257a
Slot: specify/1
Specification: <fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/spec.md
Evidence: <fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/evidence
Worktree: none (write only in the ticket directory)

Root: <fixture>/state/clones/realticket

## Repository skills (read bodies on demand)
No repository context files or indexed skills.

<invoke name="read">
<parameter name="path"><fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/spec.md</parameter>
</invoke>

<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">ls -R <fixture>/state/clones/realticket | head -30; ls <fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1</parameter>
</invoke>

<turn role="tool_result" tool="read">
# Ticket 1: Clamp a finite number

Implement a function that clamps a finite number to a range.
</turn>
<turn role="tool_result" tool="bash">
<fixture>/state/clones/realticket:
spec.md
</parameter>
</invoke>


<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">mkdir -p <fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/evidence; cd <fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1
cat > spec.md <<'E'
# Ticket 1: Clamp a finite number

## Requirements
- Export `clamp(value, min, max)` returning a number.
- Returns `min` if value < min, `max` if value > max, else `value`.
- All three args must be finite numbers (typeof number, not NaN/±Infinity); otherwise throw `TypeError`.
- If min > max, throw `RangeError`.
- `-0` handling: no special treatment required.
- Pure; no side effects or dependencies.

## Non-goals
- Non-number coercion, BigInt, arrays, infinite bounds, CLI/UI, docs.

## Acceptance criteria
1. clamp(5,0,10)=5; clamp(-1,0,10)=0; clamp(11,0,10)=10.
2. clamp(0,0,10)=0, clamp(10,0,10)=10; clamp(3,5,5)=5.
3. NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, or "1" in any arg -> TypeError.
4. clamp(1,10,0) -> RangeError.

## Verification plan
Small assertion script/test covering the cases above (node assert); run once, expect exit 0.
E
cp spec.md evidence/specify.md; cp spec.md evidence/STAGE.md</parameter>
</invoke>

<invoke name="task_transition">
<parameter name="assignmentId">4c46d82e-879d-4788-9b1b-9c8ac845257a</parameter>
<parameter name="outcome">done</parameter>
<parameter name="reason">Specification refined with exact requirements, non-goals, acceptance criteria, verification plan.</parameter>
<parameter name="evidence">["<fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/evidence/specify.md","<fixture>/state/tickets/realticket/1/evidence/STAGE.md"]</parameter>
</invoke>
